page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A1.Flex.64-128 is an ARM-based virtual machine configuration built on the Ampere Altra processor platform. The instance provides 64 dedicated physical cores running at a fixed clock speed of 3.0 GHz, with a single hardware execution thread per core. This architecture eliminates noisy-neighbor contention common to simultaneous multithreading, ensuring predictable multi-threaded throughput. System memory totals 128 GB, establishing a 1:2 core-to-memory capacity profile.

The configuration features no integrated local NVMe or solid-state storage, necessitating reliance on remote block storage volumes for persistent data. Hardware acceleration is absent, with zero GPUs provisioned. In terms of network connectivity, the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. The absence of x86-specific instruction extensions such as AVX requires applications to support the 64-bit ARM (aarch64) ISA.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the Ampere Altra platform offers high core density at favorable resource economics compared to traditional x86 processor classes. Workloads that scale horizontally across independent physical cores benefit from the linear scaling delivered by dedicated single-threaded cores. However, applications requiring massive per-thread memory allocations or fast local scratch disks may encounter architectural constraints under this specific configuration.

VM.Standard.A1.Flex.64-128 is well matched for compute-bound, parallelized services. Recommended deployments include multi-threaded software compilation, CI/CD pipeline workers, containerized microservices, video encoding, web serving pools, and general batch processing workloads designed for ARM architecture.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A1.Flex.64-128 is an arm64 compute instance powered by Ampere Altra processors operating at a sustained 3.0 GHz. The instance delivers 64 dedicated single-threaded physical cores matched with 128 GB of RAM, offering a 1:2 core-to-memory ratio designed for compute-oriented parallel processing. Because local storage is not bundled, applications must utilize external block volumes for persistent disk storage. There are no discrete GPUs included, keeping the focus entirely on dense CPU compute capacity. Each core executes a single dedicated thread, avoiding resource contention inherent to hyper-threaded designs and providing reliable, deterministic runtime performance. This platform provides strong qualitative cost efficiency for highly threaded scale-out tasks that support the ARM instruction set, such as continuous integration build clusters, containerized application clusters, web application backends, and distributed microservices.
